name: Zangwal
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page zang1255 and reference records 657257 (Decker et al. 2022) and 76828 (Shimizu 1978)
sources.note: 0 descriptive references; Glottolog's fullest description is only a wordlist; Shimizu 1978 record notes 'Sòòr = Zaŋwal [zah], Zangwal of Zungur [zah]', listed by Glottolog as an overview;comparative;wordlist, 48 pp., print (gbid j5IOAAAAYAAJ).

sources.citation: Wikipedia 'Zangwal language' (en), citing Ethnologue 18 and Moseley 2007 p.627
Caron, Bernard 2002 (review of Cosper 1999), 2005 (Les Zaars et leurs voisins), 2009 (Documenting South-Bauchi); Blench & Bulkaam 2021 Mantsi; Blench South Bauchi opening page (the Internet Archive)
sources.note: 0 hits for Zangwal in any of them; Blench's rogerblench.info B3 folder (the Internet Archive's index, 1457 urls) holds only Dyarim, Gere, Goji, Gyazi, Mantsi, Megang, Zul -- no Zangwal/Guruntum/Tala file.

sources.citation: Decker, Ken; Danladi, Yakubu; Hon, Luther; Aregbesola, Adedamola; Araokanmi, Thelma; Muniru, John; Onoja, David. 2022. A Sociolinguistic Profile of Some Endangered West Chadic B.3 Languages in South Bauchi State, Nigeria with Notes on Dulubu [dbo]. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2022-019. Dallas: SIL International. 73 pp. (SIL archives 95036)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 8.3 'Phonetic inventories' pp.25-27 gives pooled consonant/vowel charts for the seven wordlists (Zamwar has both [f] and [phi], [ngw], long vowels); sec. 8.5.1 pp.28-30 Juu/Tala/Zamwar sound correspondences; Appendix F p.50: 'The transcriptions are preliminary since there was no in-depth analysis of tones or other phonological or phonetic features.' 222-item Zamwar wordlist (Zangwar village, 2020/8/19) is tone-marked impressionistically, no stress marks. Zero hits for stress/accent/prosod/pitch. Sec. 3 p.3 lists Shimizu 1978 as the only prior work on Zamwar.
